sections.heading: Regions & ADs
items: Availability domains — the pattern: replicate across ADs for site resilience, and across fault domains inside an AD for hardware resilience. Fault domains are intra-AD resilience (independent racks, shared datacenter infrastructure), while regions are independent geographies.

Fault domains — within an AD, three fault domains group racks on different hardware, so a rack failure affects only one fault domain. Surviving a region-level event requires a second region (e.g., async replication to a paired region), not more fault domains.

Regions — realms partition OCI's global infrastructure into isolated collections of regions — the commercial realm, government realms, and others. You can subscribe to other regions for compute, storage, and networking workloads, but IAM (users, groups, compartments,…
Disaster recovery scope — match the failure scope to the isolation construct.
OCI — OCI's distributed cloud includes Dedicated Region (a complete OCI region in the customer's datacenter), Oracle Alloy (partners run their own cloud), and Roving Edge for disconnected edge sites.

Dedicated Region — is the answer for strict residency plus cloud services on-premises; a public region in the same country may satisfy residency but not the behind-the-firewall requirement. The home region is chosen at signup and is immutable: it hosts the tenancy's IAM defin…
Common trap — fault domains require 3 ADs to function; with one AD they silently do nothing.
Common trap — the home region follows the first VCN created, not the tenancy.
Common trap — a single-AD region cannot run compute instances, only storage.
Common trap — changing the home region is automatic when the billing address changes.

sections.heading: Compute
items: Compute shapes — flex shapes (VM.Standard.E4/E5/E6.Flex) let you customize the OCPU count and memory, so you pay for what the workload needs. Reserved capacity is for steady-state committed use; burstable instances handle spiky CPU on small shapes, not bulk discounts.
Flex shapes — fixed shapes come in preset sizes; bare metal gives a whole server (no hypervisor) for isolation/noisy-neighbor-sensitive workloads, not for saving money on a wiki.

Preemptible — Preemptible instances offer steep discounts because OCI may reclaim the capacity when needed — ideal for interruptible, checkpointed batch/CI workloads. OS Management Hub is the fleet patch-management service for Oracle Linux (and Windows): register instanc…
OCI Functions is the serverless platform — code runs on events (like an Object Storage upload via Events service + Notifications), scales to zero, and bills per execution.
OKE (managed Kubernetes) is for container orchestration you manage — overkill for a sporadic thumbnailer.
Common trap — flex shapes are fixed at 64 OCPUs; the only fix is terminating the tenancy.
Common trap — IAM policies can stamp out identical instances when written per-AD.
Common trap — spot markets do not exist in OCI; the only option is on-demand.
Common trap — open SSH (port 22) on the database servers' public IPs with key auth.

sections.heading: Networking (VCN)
items: VCN — VCN peering (local via LPG, or remote via DRG) routes between CIDR blocks — overlapping ranges make routes ambiguous, so OCI requires non-overlapping CIDRs (up to 5 CIDR blocks per VCN including the primary).

Security lists attach to subnets and — are stateless (return traffic needs explicit egress rules). Missing labels or disabled resolution breaks hostname lookup; security rules don't block DNS to the VCN resolver (169.254.169.254).
NSGs attach to VNICs and — are stateful (return traffic is automatically allowed), and membership follows the instance, not the subnet.
NAT gateway — a NAT gateway gives private resources outbound internet access (patch downloads) with no inbound path; instances keep no public IPs.
Common trap — internet gateway on each VCN with VPN software on an instance.
Common trap — the instances need an internet gateway for DNS.
Common trap — the CIDR is too large; peering requires /24 or smaller.
Common trap — a NAT gateway with static routes to the datacenter.

sections.heading: Storage
items: Block Volumes — provide durable, low-latency block storage for databases (attachable/detachable, with backup policies). OCI backup policies attach to block/boot volumes and run scheduled full + incremental backups to Object Storage with retention rules — the standard autom…

Object Storage tiers — a block volume attaches to one instance (multi-attach is limited/specialized); Object Storage is an object API, not POSIX file semantics. Object Storage Archive tier is the lowest-cost option for rarely-accessed data with long retention; Standard tier is fo…

Object versioning — enabling versioning on a bucket preserves earlier versions whenever an object is overwritten or deleted — you can list and restore the prior version. Pre-authenticated requests (PARs) grant scoped, expiring access to a bucket or object prefix via URL — no I…

Data protection — file Storage (NFS) suits shared file workloads, not database data files. For bulk offline ingest, OCI's Data Transfer service ships encrypted disks (or the Transfer Appliance for petabytes) to Oracle for direct upload — far faster than a thin uplink for 40 TB.
Backup policies — clones are point-in-time copies (useful for dev/test), not a backup schedule.
Block volume backups — lifecycle rules manage object retention, not volume backups.
Common trap — object Storage lifecycle rules grant temporary write access.
Common trap — they back up block volumes automatically.
Common trap — attach one volume to all 12 instances in read-write mode.
Common trap — share one boot volume across instances.

sections.heading: IAM & Security
items: Compartments are OCI's fundamental organizing and isolation unit — policies grant group permissions on specific compartments, so a compromised credential scoped to dev can't reach prod.

Least privilege — the shared model: Oracle owns security OF the cloud (facilities, hardware, virtualization, physical network); the customer owns security IN the cloud — their data classification, IAM least privilege, guest OS patching, firewall rules, and encryption choices.

Dynamic — Dynamic groups let OCI resources (instances, functions) act as principals: matching rules select them, and policies grant the dynamic group permissions — the instance authenticates with its own identity via instance principals, no stored keys.

Shared security model — cloud Guard is OCI's security-posture management: detector rules spot issues (public buckets, open security lists, etc.), and responder rules can fix them automatically. Security lists are L3/L4 packet filters (no payload inspection); NAT gateways only do o…
Cloud Guard — detection + guided response is Cloud Guard's job.
Common trap — it generates encryption keys during scans.
Common trap — oracle handles everything above the hypervisor, including customer IAM policies.
Common trap — the customer handles physical datacenter security in OCI.
Common trap — give the instance the tenancy admin's key.

sections.heading: Pricing & Governance
items: Budgets — combine quotas (quantity guardrail) with budgets (spend signal). Budgets track spend/forecast against thresholds and fire alerts (via Notifications) — they alert, they don't auto-terminate.
Cost-tracking — Cost-tracking tags let Cost Analysis slice spend by project/team/owner. Cost Analysis with compartment/tag grouping attributes spend to teams.

Cost-tracking tags — tagging resources (cost-tracking tags) is what makes the attribution work; quotas can actually cap resource counts. Require tags at creation (via policy or process) or attribution stays guesswork.
Quotas — Quotas enforce hard ceilings on how many of each resource type a compartment may contain — the backstop against runaway automation.

PAYG — the discipline: know the limits (e.g., VM counts/shapes, storage GB) because overages bill at PAYG — and check the current published terms, which Oracle can change. PAYG = no commitment, metered billing, maximum flexibility.
Common trap — always Free requires a paid support plan.
Common trap — free tier resources can't run databases.
Common trap — support tiers only differ in documentation access.
Common trap — always Free covers unlimited usage of every service for students.

checklist: Get 7–8 hours of sleep the night before — fatigue destroys recall faster than any topic gap.
Bring valid government-issued photo ID and arrive at the test center 30 minutes early.
Eat a real meal beforehand; bring water and a light snack if the center allows them.
Read every question twice before scanning the answer choices.
Flag uncertain questions and move on — return with fresh eyes at the end.
Eliminate the obviously wrong answers first, then compare the survivors.
Budget your time: answer steadily and keep a 10–15 minute review buffer.
Re-run your weakest-domain drill until mastery is at least 80%.
For Regions & ADs: restate the 'why' behind each scenario answer in your own words — if you can't explain it, you don't own it.
Redo one Compute lab from scratch without looking at the steps.
Recite the key Networking (VCN) terms from the glossary aloud from memory.
